**closeout**

- `where-was-i.py --list` is a new option. It prints the repo list, and its test passes.
- I updated `WORKFLOW.md` and `~/DEV/docs/STATUS.md`.
- Commits: skills `97a0cd7`, `1969977`, `24ce29c`, `39d71b5`. Config `15896e0`. DEV `498cea0`.

- Type `/startup` tomorrow. That is the first real run. It will also pull `house-model`, which is 2 commits behind GitHub.
- Your choice, if you want it: archive `printing-press-library` on GitHub. Then the skip line is no longer needed.

**Not checked:** I did not run a full /startup. The merge loop was tested only on scratch repos. Risk: the first real run merges all 122 repos at once. Any conflict is flagged and both versions are kept.

content.text:
**Context:** Audited and reworked the /startup, /dev-sync, and /closeout skills, then committed and pushed across the skills, config, and DEV repos.

**Key Exchanges:**
- Measured usage over the last 30 days: closeout ran in ~170 sessions, startup and dev-sync in ~20–30 each. Closeout had already been reworked on 10-25 and 10-26, so dev-sync and startup were the stale ones.
- Three skills claimed the same "where did I leave off" trigger. This overlap was found by reading where-was-i and its script options.
- A test run showed dev-sync's "memory mirror" step would copy 135 files back into the 12 archived Windows memory folders, undoing the 10-25 cleanup.
- dev-sync would have re-cloned `printing-press-library` (~66,000 files). It was trashed locally on 10-23 but still exists on GitHub.

**Decisions Made:**
- Removed the memory mirror step and its script. No other script called it.
- startup now owns the whole morning flow: sync, open board, "Picking up" report, then wait for the user. It picks the newest project worked on, because the old rule always picked the memory repo (auto-commits).
- dev-sync is sync-only. It reuses closeout's repo check, pulls all 122 repos in one pass (~10 s), and uses the auto-push hook's secret list before committing. Windows commands moved to `PLATFORMS.md` (12.7 KB → 6.6 KB). The 7-day project rule now runs only in closeout.
- dev-sync skips `printing-press-library`.
- Closeout copies deliverables to Drive `03_REPORTS` via the `gws` API instead of the Drive mount, which can hang. A "Do not use" line was added so Codex doesn't over-fire it.
- Added `where-was-i.py --list`, which prints the repo list, with a test.
- Updated `WORKFLOW.md` and `~/DEV/docs/STATUS.md`.

**Lessons Learned:**
- The shell treats `=====` as a special word, so use plain separators.
- A safety rule blocks `rm -rf`, so use a fresh folder name instead.
- A shell glob error cut a Website check short, so redo it.
- Three repos (including `printing-press-library` and `claude-global-memory`) would have shown as false "missing" on every run until their locations were checked.
- The closeout skills-check fail predated the edits: the description lacked a "Do not use" phrase.

**Action Items:**
- Run `/startup` tomorrow. It is the first real run, and it will also pull `house-model` (2 commits behind).
- Risk: the first run merges all 122 repos at once. Conflicts are flagged and both versions are kept.
- Not verified: a full /startup was never run, and the merge loop was tested only on scratch repos.
- Optional: archive `printing-press-library` on GitHub, which would make the skip line unnecessary.
- Commits: skills `97a0cd7`, `1969977`, `24ce29c`, `39d71b5`; config `15896e0`; DEV `498cea0`.
